convoLines.text: Alone, I only have to worry about one person's mistakes. Mine.
"This one — Assacu (Sandbox Tree). Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Wild Onion. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"June owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sleep's gone strange. I do push-ups at dawn at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"The fire feels smaller without June. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Did you leave someone behind? ...Sorry. You don't have to answer that. How are you holding up, though?"
Just: "Yeah." A long quiet. "Me too."
"Thank you for saying it straight. Most people perform. I'm tired of performances." You feel oddly steadier.
"This one — Ghost Pipe. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Tucumã. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." I'm an archive of a world that doesn't exist. Someone should keep the records.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Wanjiru grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time."
"Spite, mostly. Pure, clean spite at the sky. Then someone shared food with me and the spite turned into something else. I still don't have a word for the something else."
"Still on what got you through the first week."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Since June died... I keep expecting to see June at the fire. Stupid."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I taste the water before the others drink. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I asked Mabel about that question — Mabel's gone. What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
The conversation cools to something businesslike.
"Still on the worst thing you've done. Good talking."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Mabel is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"I keep turning over the last thing Mabel said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Wanjiru is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Anyway." A small smile.
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Pedro sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started. It is what it is."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Done."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Mabel owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"I should get back to it."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lastSay: d61: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Nelson Maciel is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d61: 🕯️ Nelson Maciel is dead — a stranger. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d61: What Nelson kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d61: No one is left to pick up the Codex. The village dies out — quietly, the way villages do. The season ends here.
